Term1: Concurrent Male Partner Treatment for Recurrent, Symptomatic Bacterial Vaginosis
Text:
# Concurrent Male Partner Treatment for Recurrent, Symptomatic Bacterial Vaginosis

In monogamous relationships where the female partner has confirmed symptomatic, recurrent bacterial vaginosis (defined as three or more episodes within a 12-month period), concurrent treatment of the male partner is recommended to to reduce the risk of recurrence. Concurrent treatment should be considered when the male partner is willing to complete a full 7-day treatment course.

Couples should agree to sexual abstinence or consistent condom use until both partners have completed therapy. Additionally, continued condom use for at least three months following treatment is advised to further minimize the risk of reinfection.

References:

- Concurrent Sexual Partner Therapy to Prevent Bacterial Vaginosis Recurrence.
- Obstetrics & Gynecology 146(6):p e111-e114, December 2025.
- Vodstrcil LA, et al. N Engl J Med (2025) 392:947-957.
- UpToDate (online) Bacterial vaginosis (accessed 2/10/26)
Therapy:
Metronidazole 500mg po bid x7days DI <AND> Clindamycin 2% cream apply
topically to penile skin bid x 7days [M]
